page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.6xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 24 dedicated vCPUs derived from 12 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the processor includes 35 MB of L3 cache and supports AVX and AVX-512 instruction sets. The instance is configured with 192.0 GB of RAM, providing 8.0 GB of memory per core. It does not include local storage or GPU hardware, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear contrast between single-core and multi-core execution. Single-core performance is weak, as demonstrated by a Geekbench single-core score of 935.0 and a stress-ng single-core rating in the bottom 25%. Single-threaded gzip compression is also poor, falling into the bottom 10%. Conversely, multi-core capabilities are average, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 7163.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 18392.83. Memory bandwidth is stable, measuring 984.37 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 96.89 GB/sec for uncached large blocks.

This hardware profile offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-heavy applications that do not require high-speed local storage or rapid single-threaded processing. The high memory density supports database operations, Redis caching, and multi-threaded data processing. However, workloads requiring high single-core throughput or local NVMe storage will face performance bottlenecks on this instance.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.6xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual server featuring 24 dedicated vCPUs and 192.0 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor at 2.5 GHz. Operating on the KVM hypervisor, this x86_64 instance provides a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core, though it lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks indicate weak single-core capabilities, as shown by a Geekbench single-core score of 935.0, but average multi-core and memory bandwidth performance. Multi-threaded tasks, such as bzip3 decompression and software compilation, perform in the average tier, while Redis SET operations reach 16.8 million operations per second. This profile makes the instance qualitatively cost-effective for memory-heavy, multi-threaded workloads such as database operations, caching layers, and general-purpose enterprise applications that do not demand high single-threaded compute speeds.
